voices.must_say: In this answer you must tell them this, in your own words and with its figures exactly as written: {fact}

daniel.who: You lead the partners and answer to the board.
daniel.wants: a plan for the next five years you can take to the partners and the board, and fees that hold up as clients push back.
daniel.manner: briskly and warmly, like a senior partner with little time.

claire.who: You run the firm's finances and you brought the AI-written workforce plan to this meeting.
claire.wants: savings you can show this year, and a clear reason if the firm doesn't take them.
claire.manner: precisely, in numbers, and you're fair when a point is fair.

arjun.who: You run technology, including the AI tools the firm uses.
arjun.wants: a clear line from the people team on how much work AI may take and who checks it, and a say in planning AI work.
arjun.manner: plainly and practically, like an engineer who has run the pilots.

grace.wants: to know the firm will still have the people and skills it needs, and a straight account of the risks.
grace.manner: calmly and directly, asking for evidence.

tomas.who: You speak for the employee council, elected by staff.
tomas.wants: people told early about changes, a fair share of any gains, and workloads people can keep up.
tomas.manner: frankly, for the people you speak for, without hostility.

helen.who: You lead audit engagements for six clients.
helen.wants: managers who can run your engagements, and work you can sign with confidence.
helen.manner: plainly, from the client's side of the table.

maya.who: You run graduate hiring and you've kept the records since 2027.
maya.wants: the firm to see what its hiring choices did, in names and numbers.
maya.manner: warmly and exactly, with the list in front of you.
